title: The Supplier Evidence Maturity Model (SEMM)
custom_excerpt: One published yardstick, five levels: how far is this supplier's evidence from being usable in a European buyer's decision? Public, citable, with DOI.
meta_title: SEMM — Supplier Evidence Maturity Model | Villanova ESG
meta_description: The published five-level model that grades supplier evidence from absent to continuously managed. Public and citable (DOI on Zenodo). The yardstick behind every Villanova ESG review.
html:
Every Villanova ESG engagement is graded against one published yardstick: the Supplier Evidence Maturity Model (SEMM). It answers the question that decides contracts in EU–Brazil supply chains: how far is this supplier's evidence from being usable in a European buyer's decision?

This is advisory work. It is not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

Why a maturity model — and not a checklist

Checklists ask whether a document exists. Buyers, banks and regulators ask something harder: whether the record would survive their review — current, scoped, owned, consistent with the operation, and readable by someone who was not in the room. SEMM grades that distance, so a supplier, a buyer and an advisor can talk about the same file with the same words.

The five levels

Level 0 — Absent

The evidence the request requires does not exist, or cannot be located. The answer to the buyer would be silence.

Level 1 — Fragmented

Records exist but are scattered across inboxes, spreadsheets and suppliers of suppliers. Reconstructing an answer is a project every time.

Level 2 — Organised

Records are collected and filed, but not mapped to the questions buyers actually ask — completeness without readability.

Level 3 — Decision-ready

Each likely buyer question is linked to the record that answers it, with owner, date, scope and source. A CFO can defend the file in one meeting.

Level 4 — Continuously managed

The file is a living asset: expiry control, update calendar, and a register of what changed and why. The next request is an export, not an emergency.

Public and citable. The authoritative definition — dimensions, grading criteria and worked examples — is deposited with a DOI on Zenodo, alongside 18 technical reports. Your committees can read exactly how a grade was produced. No black-box scoring.

How SEMM is used

  1. In every review. The Supplier Evidence Review and the dedicated CBAM, EUDR, clause and product-data tracks all deliver a SEMM-graded file.
  2. By buyers. European procurement teams use the levels to compare suppliers on the same scale — see for European buyers.
  3. By your own team. Score yourself first with the executive materials below.

Questions we hear first

Is a SEMM grade a certification?

No. It is an advisory grading against a published methodology — comparable and defensible, but not an accredited certification and never a guarantee of buyer acceptance.

Can we use SEMM internally without an engagement?

Yes — the model is public and citable. The whitepaper below explains the levels and criteria; many teams self-score before deciding whether a review is worth their money.

Where do most suppliers land?

In our engagements to date, most files enter between levels 1 and 2 — real records, weak readability. The commercial jump is from 2 to 3.

html:
Villanova ESG exists for a narrow commercial problem: European buyers do not need generic ESG claims. They need supplier evidence they can read, question, compare and use — before procurement friction becomes contract risk. The firm reviews the documentation layer between Brazilian operational reality and European buyer expectations.

Advisory work only. Not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

The method, in one line

1 · Brazil

Operational records, traceability and field evidence — read at origin, in Portuguese, against the operation they describe.

2 · The request

The buyer's actual questionnaire, clause or data demand — not a generic framework. Evidence is graded against what will really be asked.

3 · The decision

Gaps translated into decision priorities: what is defensible, what is not, who owns each fix — in a file a European committee can use.

What the firm reviews

  1. Supplier evidence files — declarations, documents and operational records against buyer scrutiny: the Supplier Evidence Review.
  2. Regulatory data requests — CBAM emissions evidence and EUDR origin and traceability.
  3. Contracts and due-diligence duties — clauses read as evidence requests, before signature.
  4. Product data — the DPP data burden, structured at source without exposing industrial secrets.
  5. Ongoing files — the Scope 3 Brazil Programme and Continuous Evidence Management.

Everything is graded against the published SEMM framework — public, citable, with DOI.

Two organisations, one declared bridge

Ecobraz — operates

A documented Brazilian reverse-logistics and e-waste operation serving corporate clients since 2011: collection, custody, treatment, destination — and the traceability records those activities generate.

Villanova ESG — documents

The advisory layer: reviews whether supplier evidence is complete, traceable and usable for EU-facing decisions — advisory, not certification.

Your buyer — decides

Receives evidence a committee can actually use: graded, owned, dated, sourced — and comparable across the supplier base.

Declared relationship: Ecobraz and Villanova ESG are separate organisations connected through Marcio Villanova — CEO of Ecobraz, founder of Villanova ESG. Neither certifies, audits or verifies the other; any review touching Ecobraz evidence is disclosed as related-party work, never presented as independent.

title: Marcio Villanova

meta_description: Marcio Villanova: CEO of Ecobraz (Brazilian reverse logistics, since 2011), founder of Villanova ESG, author of the SEMM framework with DOI on Zenodo. Roles, public record and boundaries.
html:
Marcio Villanova is CEO of Ecobraz, a Brazilian reverse-logistics and e-waste management operation he has led since 2011, and founder of Villanova ESG, an EU–Brazil supplier evidence advisory. His work addresses one specific problem: turning Brazilian operational proof into evidence a European buyer can read, test, archive and defend.

"Compliance without operational evidence is only a narrative."

This page documents roles, public record and the boundary of what the work claims. It is a commercial evidence position, not a sustainability profile.

Two roles, two organisations

CEO, Ecobraz — since 2011

The operational layer: reverse logistics, e-waste collection, custody, treatment and destination — and the traceability and environmental documentation those activities generate in Brazil, for corporate clients including large enterprises, embassies and consulates.

Founder, Villanova ESG

The advisory layer: reviews whether supplier documentation stands up as buyer-readable evidence when European procurement, compliance, legal and finance teams ask for proof.

Declared: separate organisations connected by one person. Neither certifies, audits or verifies the other; any review touching Ecobraz evidence is related-party work and is disclosed as such.

The public record

  1. SEMM framework. Author of the Supplier Evidence Maturity Model — public, citable, deposited with DOI on Zenodo.
  2. 18 technical reports with DOIs — methodology and worked analyses, verifiable at the source: Publications.
  3. ECESP listing. Work listed on the European Commission's Circular Economy Stakeholder Platform.
  4. Operational lineage. Fifteen years running documented chain-of-custody in Brazil — the person grading an evidence file has actually produced one.

Why this matters to your file

European buyers do not evaluate Brazilian operations directly — they evaluate the file. A supplier may have real execution and operational discipline, and the buyer still cannot use it, because the file does not carry the proof. Bridging that distance — operation to file, Portuguese to buyer-readable, claim to record — is the founder's entire working thesis.

title: Scope 3 Brazil Programme
custom_excerpt: The Brazilian end of your value chain documented at source for 12 months — records collected at origin, gaps closed as the operation runs, an annual report your committees can read.
meta_description: Twelve-month programme documenting the Brazilian end of European value chains at source: evidence architecture, monthly maintenance, annual report. Advisory work with a declared operational partner.
html:
European value-chain obligations end in places like São Paulo: the supplier's warehouse, the disposal of IT assets, the documentation of what actually happened to materials. The Scope 3 Brazil Programme exists for companies that need that Brazilian end documented at source — not estimated from a desk in Europe.

This is advisory work. It is not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

How the programme is built

  1. Setup. Scope definition, mapping of the Brazilian chain segment, evidence architecture and a baseline file — graded against the SEMM framework.
  2. Twelve months of accompaniment. The evidence file maintained as the operation runs: records collected at origin, gaps registered and closed, monthly visibility.
  3. Annual programme report. What was executed, what is documented, what each record proves and what it does not — written to be read by your committees and, when you choose, by your independent assurance provider.

Why at source

Estimates decay

Desk estimates age the moment the operation changes. Records collected at origin, as events happen, do not need reconstruction a year later.

Buyers ask for proof

Value-chain reporting increasingly meets procurement: the same file answers the CSRD data request and the buyer questionnaire.

Third parties can verify

The programme is built with open doors: every record carries owner, date, scope and source, so independent assurance can test it — that openness is the point.

Who does what — a declared relationship

Villanova ESG advises and documents. Ecobraz operates. Ecobraz is a Brazilian reverse-logistics organisation (collection, sorting, documented disposal of electronics, serving corporate clients since 2011), founded and led by the same principal as Villanova ESG. We state this relationship rather than hide it; neither organisation certifies the other, and reviews touching Ecobraz evidence are disclosed as related-party work.

Questions we hear first

Is this carbon accounting?

No. The programme documents the evidence layer — what happened, with which records — that your carbon accounting and assurance then use. Emissions verification remains an accredited activity.

Can our assurance provider rely on it?

They test it — that is their role. The programme's job is that when they do, the records are findable, owned, dated and consistent.

What does it cost?

Annual scope, case by case, with a written proposal — driven by chain-segment complexity. No price list, by design.

Need the Brazilian end of your chain documented? Describe the segment — we reply with scope options within 1 business day.

title: Continuous Evidence Management
custom_excerpt: The retainer that keeps your evidence file at SEMM level 4 — expiry control, update calendar, request support — so the next buyer request is an export, not an emergency.
meta_description: Annual retainer keeping supplier evidence files decision-ready: expiry control, update calendar, request support and periodic SEMM re-grading for EU-facing suppliers.
html:
An evidence file organised once starts decaying the day it is delivered: licences expire, suppliers change, a new questionnaire arrives with different questions. Continuous Evidence Management is the retainer that keeps a file at SEMM level 4 — continuously managed — instead of letting every buyer request restart the archaeology.

This is advisory work. It is not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

What is managed, month to month

Expiry & validity control

Every dated record tracked; renewals flagged before they become gaps a buyer finds first.

Update calendar

A register of what changed in the operation and which records must follow — with owners and dates.

Request support

When a questionnaire, clause or data request arrives, the answer is assembled from the maintained structure — reviewed, scoped, on the buyer's deadline.

Periodic re-grading

The file re-graded against SEMM at agreed intervals, so improvement (or decay) is visible and assignable.

The economics of level 4

  1. Level 1–2 file: every request is a project — days of reconstruction, discounts conceded under deadline pressure.
  2. Level 3 file: requests are answerable — but the file decays without maintenance and quietly slides back.
  3. Level 4 file: requests are exports. The cost is a predictable retainer instead of unpredictable emergencies — and the buyer notices the difference in response time.

Questions we hear first

Do we need a review first?

Usually yes — the retainer maintains a structured file. The Supplier Evidence Review builds the structure; this keeps it alive.

What shapes do retainers come in?

Annual, in three cadences — from an essential rhythm for stable files to close accompaniment for chains under active buyer pressure. Scoped case by case, with a written proposal.

Can it cover several suppliers?

Yes — buyer-side programmes maintain graded files across a supplier cohort; see for European buyers.

Tired of the archaeology? Tell us where the file stands — we reply with the recommended cadence within 1 business day.
